title: TransFuser: Imitation with Transformer-Based Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving
layout_note: Ladder layout: inside a large framed 'TransFuser' box, an Image Branch band (top) and a BEV Branch band (bottom) each run four encoder stages left to right; four green Transformer boxes sit in the gap between the bands as rungs exchanging features with both. Outputs of both branches merge at a sum node right of the frame, then a short row (512 vector -> MLP -> 64 vector -> chain of four GRU cells) produces waypoints; a dashed zoom panel at top right expands one Transformer.
grouping: An outer thin-framed rectangle titled 'TransFuser' holds two grey-tinted horizontal bands labelled in bold at their right ends ('Image Branch', 'BEV Branch'); the shared fusion transformers sit on white between them. The detail panel is a light-green box with a dashed grey frame and dashed zoom lines from the last Transformer, echoing its green fill; goal-location conditioning is a green-outlined bar under the GRU row.
shapes_depth: Encoder stages are flat trapezoids in a distinct pastel per stage (yellows/peach/pink on top, teal/blues below), each followed by a small 3-D cuboid feature map with its size printed (e.g. 176 x 40 x 72, 64 x 64 x 72); sum nodes are circled plus signs; Transformer, AvgPool+FC and MLP are flat square-cornered boxes; the detail panel draws tokens as small multicolour stacked cubes around a vertical Self-Attention bar; GRU cells are small grey boxes.
proposed_highlight: The fusion Transformers are the only green elements and repeat four times as rungs between the two branches; the last one is expanded in a green dashed zoom panel with an x L marker, and the whole fusion backbone is boxed and titled 'TransFuser'.
lesson: Draw two-sensor fusion as a ladder: two tinted branch bands with matching stage-by-stage feature cuboids, and the fusion module repeated as same-coloured rungs between them, one rung zoomed into a tinted detail panel in the corner.
notes: venue = arXiv (remembered venue: IEEE TPAMI 2023, the journal extension of the CVPR 2021 'Multi-Modal Fusion Transformer' paper; not printed on the arXiv first page); year = arXiv preprint year. Auxiliary losses are drawn separately in Fig 3; this figure shows only the backbone and the GRU waypoint decoder. Notation in the GRU row (delta w_1..w_4, w_1..w_3, (0,0)) is drawn as small math labels.

taxonomy.task: end-to-end driving waypoint prediction from camera and LiDAR

core.what: two horizontal lanes - an Image Branch fed by an RGB photo above, a BEV Branch fed by a LiDAR bird's-eye image below - with a row of four green Transformer boxes between them, each taking a vertical arrow from both lanes and returning a vertical arrow into a circled plus on each lane, once per resolution

relations.form: two grey bands stacked inside a 'TransFuser' frame, each a left-to-right chain of trapezoid conv blocks and feature cubes labelled with sizes (176x40x72 ... 22x5x1512 on top, 64x64x72 ... 8x8x1512 below), ending in AvgPool + FC
four Transformer boxes sit in the gap between the lanes, aligned under the four stages, with straight vertical arrows down/up from each lane into the box and back to that lane's circled plus

dashed grey lines run from the last Transformer box to a green-tinted panel at the upper right showing image and BEV token cubes (H1xW1xC1, H2xW2xC2) flattened into one stack, through Self-Attention, and split back, 'x L'
the two lanes' pooled outputs converge by diagonal lines on one circled plus outside the frame, then a 512 bar -> MLP -> 64 bar
four GRU cells unrolled left to right, each emitting a waypoint offset delta-w_i above and taking the previous waypoint below, with green dashed arrows from a 'Goal Location' box feeding every cell

channels.colour: warm yellows to pinks = image-branch blocks, cool teals to blues = BEV-branch blocks (hue = modality, shade changes per stage without stated meaning); green = transformer fusion, but green also fills the Goal Location box and its dashed arrows; the token cubes in the zoom panel are multicoloured cells
channels.shape: trapezoids = conv stages; 3D cubes = feature maps with their sizes; rectangles = transformers and heads; tall thin bars = feature vectors; circled plus = element-wise sum
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow; green dashed arrows = goal-location conditioning; dashed grey lines = zoom tie
channels.frame: one large outlined frame = the TransFuser backbone; grey bands = the two branches; a dashed-outlined green panel = transformer detail

quality.strengths: the multi-scale fusion is geometry: two equal lanes with the transformers in the corridor between them, one per resolution, connected by short straight vertical arrows; real inputs (a night street photo and a LiDAR BEV raster) start each lane, and every feature cube carries its size; the waypoint decoder is unrolled into four GRU steps
quality.weaknesses: the transformer detail panel, which explains how the two modalities are fused, is the smallest and densest element at the far right edge; green means both 'fusion transformer' and 'goal location'; the shade changes along each lane look meaningful but are not; the pooled outputs leave the frame on diagonals to a sum node that sits outside the backbone

insights.structure: Two grey branch bands (image above, LiDAR BEV below) inside one titled frame are tied together by four green Transformer rungs at matching stages, and a separate waypoint decoder row and a dashed detail panel sit outside the frame on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are a wide dark RGB frame and a square black LiDAR BEV image at the left edge, each stage's feature map is a coloured cuboid with its exact C x H x W printed beside it, and the fused vectors are thin upright bars labelled 512 and 64.
insights.emphasis: Green is reserved for the fusion transformers and their zoomed detail panel (with an 'x L' repeat marker), so the contribution reads as the repeated element bridging two otherwise pastel branches.
insights.flow: Thin black lines run straight left to right along each band through circled-plus nodes, short vertical arrows go up and down between bands and rungs, the two branch outputs converge diagonally to one sum node, and the GRU chain steps right with green dashed arrows rising from a Goal Location bar.
insights.avoid: Lines are hairline-thin and the GRU/goal row plus the detail panel's token cubes are tiny relative to the frame, so the output stage and the attention mechanism are hard to read at column size.

arrangement.units: a large titled frame holding two grey-tinted branch lanes with four rungs between them; outside it, a waypoint-decoder row at bottom right and a dashed light-green detail panel at top right
arrangement.inputs_as: real sensor images: an RGB camera frame and a LiDAR BEV render, each with a two-line label above
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the GRU chain ends in delta-w waypoint outputs
arrangement.shared: each fusion Transformer is drawn once between the bands with arrows to and from both branches

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
